problem: A parcel delivery company records whether each delivered package requires a signature upon arrival. On average, $9$ out of $50$ packages require a signature. Each package's status is independent of the others. Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability that the first package requiring a signature is the fifth package delivered or later is{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of packages delivered until a package that requires a signature is delivered. On average, the chance that any single package requires a signature is 

$$
p=\frac{9}{50}=0.18.
$$

So, the number of packages until the first package that requires a signature is delivered can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success $p=0.18.$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.18).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={(1-0.18)}^{x-1}(0.18) \\  & ={(0.82)}^{x-1}(0.18)\end{aligned}
$$

To compute $P(X\ge 5),$ we will use the complement:

$$
P(X\ge 5)=1-P(X<5)
$$

Computing the probability of the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<5) & =P(X\in {1,2,3,4}) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4) \\  & =(0.82)^{1-1}(0.18)+(0.82)^{2-1}(0.18)+(0.82)^{3-1}(0.18)+(0.82)^{4-1}(0.18) \\  & =(0.18)+(0.82)(0.18)+(0.82)^{2}(0.18)+(0.82)^{3}(0.18) \\  & =[1+0.82+(0.82)^{2}+(0.82)^{3}](0.18) \\  & ≈0.548,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Therefore, the probability that at least $4$ packages are delivered before the first package that requires a signature is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 5) & =1-P(X<5) \\  & ≈1-0.548 \\  & ≈0.452,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
